You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 8f6b8ed3b02e3202b062a0d786c1c623f64cad63 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2018 13:17:49 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] staging: wilc1000: fix incorrect allocation size for
 structure

Currently the allocation for str_vals is for the sizeof the pointer
rather than the size of the structure.  Fix this.

Detected by smatch
"wilc_wlan_cfg_init() error: not allocating enough data 392 vs 8"

Fixes: acceb12a9f8b ("staging: wilc1000: refactor code to avoid static variables for config parameters")
Signed-off-by: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
---
 drivers/staging/wilc1000/wilc_wlan_cfg.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/staging/wilc1000/wilc_wlan_cfg.c b/drivers/staging/wilc1000/wilc_wlan_cfg.c
index 930a3896f4ae..faa001c75681 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/wilc1000/wilc_wlan_cfg.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/wilc1000/wilc_wlan_cfg.c
@@ -457,7 +457,7 @@ int wilc_wlan_cfg_init(struct wilc *wl)
 	if (!wl->cfg.s)
 		goto out_w;
 
-	str_vals = kzalloc(sizeof(str_vals), GFP_KERNEL);
+	str_vals = kzalloc(sizeof(*str_vals), GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!str_vals)
 		goto out_s;
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by allocating memory for the `str_vals` variable using the size of the pointer itself instead of the size of the actual structure it was intended to hold. This resulted in insufficient memory being allocated, leading to potential memory corruption or access violations when the program attempted to use `str_vals`. The patch corrected the allocation to use the size of the structure, ensuring that enough memory is allocated for the intended data.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by allocating memory for the `str_vals` variable using the size of the pointer itself instead of the size of the actual structure it was intended to hold. This resulted in insufficient memory being allocated, leading to potential memory corruption or access violations when the program attempted to use `str_vals`. The patch corrected the allocation to use the size of the structure, ensuring that enough memory is allocated for the intended data.
